title: X3 Configure the Project

description: Add three justified milestones, copy and link a preconfigured Project, decide priorities and dates, and record one blocking dependency.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- **Time:** 40 minutes
- **You produce:** three milestones with justified dates; a Project, copied from the showcase and linked to your repository; your six sub-issues in it, with the priorities and dates that you chose; and one "blocked by" dependency.
- **New terms:** [Project](../cheat-sheet.qmd#project), [milestone](../cheat-sheet.qmd#milestone), [view](../cheat-sheet.qmd#view), [field](../cheat-sheet.qmd#field), [Project workflow](../cheat-sheet.qmd#project-workflow), [dependency](../cheat-sheet.qmd#dependency). All terms are in the [cheat sheet](../cheat-sheet.qmd).
:::

## Why this step

Issues describe the work. A **Project** shows the work as a plan: what is waiting, what is in progress, and what happens when. A Project belongs to your account, not to the repository. You link it to the repository, and you set its **visibility separately**. A public repository can have a private Project, and the reverse.

A plan needs time. GitHub offers two different tools for time, and they answer different questions. A **milestone** groups Issues under one due date in the repository: "What must be ready for the registration?" **Date fields** in the Project give each Issue a start and a target: "When do I work on this?" The **roadmap** shows both together. Milestones and the roadmap form a phase plan; the board adds a Kanban view of the daily work ([Approaches](../approaches.qmd)).

Order matters too. "Submit the registration" cannot start before "Check the registration requirements" ends. This is a **dependency** ("blocked by"), not a hierarchy. A parent-child relation says "this is part of that"; a dependency says "this waits for that". Keep the two apart.

The fields and the views are the same for every thesis, so you copy them from the showcase Project. The decisions stay with you: the priorities, the dates, and the justification of each milestone. Milestone dates need a justification. The fictional registration (2026-12-01) and submission (2027-06-01) stand in for official dates of the Dean's Office; the six months between them follow the [DH study plan, Art. 15 Abs. 4](../../documentation/requirements.qmd). The middle milestone is your own estimate, and you may move it. Never move an official date silently.

## Before you start

- You finished [X2](x2.qmd).
- Open the [showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11) in a second tab.

## Steps

### Create the milestones

1. Click **Issues**, then **Milestones**, then **New milestone**.
2. Type the title `M1 Registration submitted` and the due date `2026-12-01`.
3. In **Description**, write the justification. The [milestones of the example repository](https://github.com/maehr/projm-example-thesis/milestones?state=all) show one for each date.
4. Click **Create milestone**.
5. Repeat for `M2 Data documented and validated` (2027-03-01, proposed) and `M3 Thesis submitted` (2027-06-01).
6. Open each sub-issue and set its milestone in the sidebar: E01 tasks → M1, E08-S1 and E08-T2 → M2, E08-T3 → M3.

{{< screenshot x3-milestones >}}

### Copy the Project

1. Open the [showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11).
2. Click **…** (top right), then **Make a copy**.
3. Under **Owner**, select your account.
4. Type the name `PROJM thesis plan`. Do not select **Draft issues**.
5. Click **Copy project**. The copy opens. It has the views, the fields, and the workflows of the showcase, but no Issues.

{{< screenshot x3-make-a-copy >}}

### Link the Project and set its visibility

1. Open your repository. Click **Projects**, then **Link a project**.
2. Select `PROJM thesis plan` and click **Save**.
3. Open the Project. Click **…**, then **Settings**.
4. Under **Danger zone**, check **Visibility**. A copy starts **private**. Select **Public** only on the public path.
5. Pair: click **Manage access**. Invite your partner with the role **Write**. Access to the repository does not include access to the Project.

{{< screenshot x3-manage-access >}}

### Add the Issues

1. In the Project table, click **+** at the bottom (or press `Ctrl`+`Space`).
2. Type `#`, select your repository, and select the epic E01.
3. Repeat for E08.
4. The workflow **Auto-add sub-issues to project** adds the six sub-issues. New items get the Status **Backlog**. If a sub-issue is missing, add it the same way.

### Decide the priorities and the dates

This step is planning, not copying. You decide, and you can explain each value.

1. For each sub-issue, set **Priority** (`High`, `Normal`, or `Low`) and **Basis** (`Rule`, `Practice`, or `Demo`).
2. Set a **Start date** and a **Target date** for each sub-issue. Each target date must lie before the due date of its milestone.
3. Let E01-T3 start after the target date of E01-T1. E01-T3 waits for E01-T1.
4. Open milestone M2. Add one sentence to its description: why this date, and what happens if it moves.
5. Compare your values with the [Backlog view of the showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11/views/1). Your values can differ. You must be able to justify them.

### Check the workflows

1. In the Project header, click **Workflows**.
2. Check that six workflows have a green dot.
3. Check two of them: **Pull request linked to issue** sets the Status **In review**, and **Item closed** sets the Status **Done**. X4 depends on both.

{{< screenshot x3-copy-workflows >}}

### Record the dependency

1. Open `E01-T3 Submit the thesis registration to the Dean's Office`.
2. In the sidebar, click the gear icon next to **Relationships**.
3. Select **Mark as blocked by**, then select `E01-T1`. Close the list.
4. Check that the pill "Blocked by: E01-T1" appears under the title.
5. Optional: mark `E08-T3` as blocked by `E08-T2`.

### Optional: build a Project yourself

Do this after the workshop, or if the copy fails. It shows how the copied Project works.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Build the fields, views, and workflows by hand"}

1. In your repository, click **Projects**, then **New project**. Select **Table** and name the Project.
2. In the table header, click **+** and select **New field**. Create `Priority` (single select: `High`, `Normal`, `Low`), `Basis` (single select: `Rule`, `Practice`, `Demo`), `Start date`, and `Target date` (date).
3. Open the settings of the field **Status**. Set the options to `Backlog`, `Ready`, `In progress`, `In review`, `Done`.
4. Rename the first view to `Backlog`. Click **New view**, select **Board**, name it `Board`, and type `-label:kind:epic` in the filter.
5. Click **New view**, select **Roadmap**, and name it `Roadmap`. Click **Date fields** and select `Start date` and `Target date`. Click **Markers** and select **Milestone**. Set the zoom to **Quarter**.
6. Click **View**, then **Save view**, then **Save** in the confirmation dialog.
7. Click **Workflows**. Select **Pull request linked to issue**, click **Edit**, and set the value `Status: In review`. Save the workflow and turn it on.

Change the Status options before you rely on the workflows. A workflow that used a renamed option stops with an error. Open **Workflows** and select the new option again.

{{< screenshot x3-workflows-broken >}}

{{< screenshot x3-roadmap-date-fields >}}

:::

## Expected state

{{< screenshot x3-backlog >}}

{{< screenshot x3-board >}}

{{< screenshot x3-roadmap >}}

- [ ] Three milestones exist; each has a due date and a justification.
- [ ] The Project is linked to the repository and has the visibility you chose.
- [ ] Your six sub-issues are in the Project, each with a Priority, a Basis, a Start date, and a Target date.
- [ ] Each target date lies before the due date of its milestone.
- [ ] The Roadmap shows bars and the milestone markers.
- [ ] E01-T3 shows "Blocked by: E01-T1".

## If something goes wrong

| Problem | Cause | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Make a copy** is missing. | You are not signed in, or you opened the Project from a phone. | Sign in. Use a desktop browser. |
| The copy is private, but you chose the public path. | A copy always starts private. | **…** → **Settings** → **Danger zone** → **Visibility**. |
| Your partner cannot see the Project. | Repository access does not include Project access. | **…** → **Settings** → **Manage access** → invite the partner with the role Write. |
| The sub-issues do not appear. | The epic was added before the workflow ran, or the workflow is off. | Add each sub-issue with **+** and `#`. Check **Workflows**. |
| The Project does not appear in the repository. | It is not linked. | **Projects** tab → **Link a project**. |
| The roadmap shows "Your project needs at least one date or iteration field". | The view has no date fields selected. | Select the date fields in **Date fields**. |
| The view settings are lost after a reload. | The changes were not saved. | Click **View → Save view**, then **Save** in the dialog. A blue dot means unsaved changes. |
| No gear icon next to **Relationships**. | The page has not finished loading. | Reload the Issue page and wait. |
| Time runs out. | — | Skip the second dependency and the M2 justification. Add them during X6. |

## Alternatives

- **Pair:** one person copies and links the Project and invites the partner; the other creates the milestones. Decide the priorities and the dates together.
- **Private path:** keep the copy private. Project visibility does not follow the repository visibility.
